 Shri V. V. Goutam with Shri Abhishek Tugnawat - advocat  petitioner.

sentences.text: Shri Sudeep Bhargava appearing on behalf of Advocate Ge  ORDER 1.

This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following reliefs:-
"a) To allow this petition by issuing appropriate writ, direction or order, and quash the impugned notification dated 03/09/2024 issued under Section 11(1) of Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, qua petitioner society, and b) Pass any other relief which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the interest of justice."
2. The grievance of the petitioner is that respondent No.2/Collector and Ex- officio Deputy Secretary, M.P. Govt. Revenue Department, District Ujjain has issued the notification dated 03/09/2024 for acquisition of land situated at Ujjain for a total area of 38.91 hectare of land without following due process of law.

3. Shri V.V. Goutam, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is already running a medical college and in the process of setting up NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:31524 2 WP-34288-2024 Medical Complex which includes Medical college,
dental college, college of nursing, college of para medical science etc. which would generate substantial employment in the area, whereas the notification dated 03/09/2024 has been challenged on the ground that before issuance of the notification, the Collector has not adhered to the pre-conditions prescribed for issuance of such notification.

Counsel has also submitted that respondent No.2 has also not complied with provisions of Sections 2(2), 8, 10 and 11 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 2013') and thus, it is submitted that the Collector has acted in excess of the jurisdiction in issuing the aforesaid notification.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Shri Sudeep Bhargava, learned counsel for the respondents, on the other hand has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the aforesaid notification itself has been issued by respondent No.2 in order to call for the objections as provided under Section 11 of the Act of 2013, and in such circumstances, the petition is premature and not maintainable.

It is further submitted that since the Collector is competent to hear the objections, the petition is liable to be dismissed, and the petitioner can still file his objections as in the impugned Notification, the period for filing the objection is 60 days.

Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the documents filed on record,
it is apparent that the impugned notification dated 03/09/2024 has been issued by respondent No.2 while exercising its powers under Section 11 of the Act of 2013, which provides for publication of preliminary notification, and the objections have been invited from the concerned persons as provided under Section 15 of the Act of 2013.

Thus, at this juncture, it is not known if the Collector has complied with all the provisions of law or not, and that NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:31524 3 WP-34288-2024 is why the aforesaid provision of opportunity of hearing has been enshrined in the Act of 2013 so as to call the objections from the aggrieved persons.

In such circumstances, when the law regarding land acquisition itself is a self contained Act, this Court does not find it to be a fit case to exercise its extraordinary writ jurisdiction to forestall/preempt the process, which the Collector, Ujjain has initiated.

This Court is also of the considered opinion that whatever objections the petitioner has raised in this petition, can very well be raised before the Collector who is competent to decide the same, and if the petitioner is aggrieved by the order of the Collector, it can resort to the remedy available under law.
6. In view of the same, the admission is declined, the writ petition is hereby dismissed in limine .

However, with liberty reserved to the petitioner to file the objections before the Collector within a further period of 15 days, on or before 22/11/2024, and if the objections are filed by the petitioner,
the same shall be decided by the Collector, in accordance with law as envisaged under the Act of 2013.
It is made clear that this Court has not reflected upon the merits of the case.
